title: France – Exhibition centre construction work – Concession de service public pour l’exploitation du centre de congrès et parc d’expositions « Mégacité » et la réalisation de travaux d’extension et de rénovation
description: Implanté sur 35 000 m², MEGACITE est un pôle évènementiel qui permet l’organisation en intérieur et en extérieur de manifestations de type salons, congrès, séminaires, expositions, spectacles, etc. Construit en 1984, une extension du bâtiment a été réalisée en 2006. Il comprend principalement un ensemble d’espaces composé d’un amphithéâtre de 986 places, 4 halls d’expositions de 3800 m², 2400 m², 1800 m² et 1135 m², un espace polyvalent d’accueil de 600 m², 7 salles d’atelier de 30 à 300 personnes, un bar, des cuisines, des aires extérieures permettant l’implantation de chapiteaux. L’extension ouverte en 2006 comprend un amphithéâtre supplémentaire de 350 places, 2 salles d’atelier (70 et 90 places), une salle de presse, un espace de bureau dédié aux organisateurs. Compte tenu de l’état du site, le prochain contrat mettra à la charge du concessionnaire la construction d’une halle modulaire de 5000 à 8000 m² destinée aux foires, salons, expositions et congrès comprenant un office restauration ainsi que la rénovation des espaces actuels. Le coût du projet est estimé entre 18 et 23,5 M€TTC. La construction de cette halle modulaire impliquera la démolition et le réaménagement d’une partie des infrastructures qui feront l’objet de travaux pris en charge par Amiens Métropole qui auront lieu après 2032. Enfin, l’exploitation des espaces mutualisés du Quai de l’innovation sera intégrée en option dans le périmètre de la concession. Cet équipement est situé au cœur du quartier historique St Leu et comporte des espaces mutualisés représentant environ 1 900 m² incluant des salles de réunions, des salles de conférence gradinées de 50 à 300 places ainsi que des espaces de bureau, de réception, de coworking et de visio-conférence. Durée du contrat La durée de 180 mois est la durée minimum du contrat. Selon les projets des candidats et l’économie générale des offres, cette durée pourra être portée à 240 mois maximum. Conditions d’exécution de la concession Le concessionnaire percevra directement les recettes d’exploitation et supportera directement les charges du service sur la durée du contrat. Amiens Métropole versera une subvention d’investissement plafonnée à 70% du coût total des investissements. Le cas échéant, la collectivité versera au concessionnaire une contribution financière afin de prendre en compte le niveau des missions de service public qu'elle entend lui imposer Par ailleurs, la convention prévoira les modalités d’un intéressement dans l’hypothèse où le résultat dégagé par le concessionnaire serait supérieur à ses prévisions. Informations complémentaires La description des prestations ainsi que la liste des pièces à fournir par les candidats figurent dans la pièce intitulée "Informations complémentaires candidats Mégacité".

title: The National ALS Registry Expansion of Outreach and Awareness to Persons with ALS in Select States Covered by the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Association
description: The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Association for the project titled "The National ALS Registry Expansion of Outreach and Awareness to Persons with ALS in Select States covered by the ALS Association." The contract will promote and enroll patients into the National ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis) Registry by providing continuous outreach, education, awareness (e.g., facilitate ALS patient computer access to the National ALS Registry web portal; provide educational materials; use social media, etc.) to persons with ALS, their families, caregivers, and researchers. These activities will be directed in the states of: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, California � Sacramento Area, Florida, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wisconsin. The ALS Association is uniquely qualified to fulfill this requirement because it possesses a combination of national ALS clinical infrastructure, credentialing authority, research engagement, and established patient and provider relationships that is not available from any other organization. This contract action is for services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, and is justified under 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1). This notice of intent to sole source is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received within 15 of days of the issuance of this notice shall be considered by the government. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any quotation/response should be emailed to uwo8@cdc.gov by the posted deadline.

title: Netherlands – Winter-maintenance materials – Inkoop advies en materieel gladheidsbestrijding
description: De scope van de opdracht is het samen met de opdrachtgever voorbereiden van de gladheidsbestrijding, het leveren en onderhouden van het benodigd materieel en materiaal voor de gladheidsbestrijding en het ondersteunen bij de uitvoering van de gladheidsbestrijding. Om een versnipperde inkoop te voorkomen is gekozen voor een opgavegerichte aanpak. Buiten deze inkoop vallen: o Het leveren van zout en pekel; o Het coördineren en uitvoeren van gladheidsbestrijding; o Het beheer en onderhoud van de gemeentelijke wegdekmeetpunten; o Het leveren van Meteorologische ondersteuning. - Een nieuw gladheidsbestrijdingsplan (beleid en operationeel) opstellen en implementeren; - Levering/huur/lease etc. van vervangende wintermachines: gemeentelijke vloot van wintermachines actueel houden (operationeel, bedrijfszeker); - Routebegeleidingssystemen en voertuigtracking: implementeren, efficiënt en operationeel houden; - Kennisniveau medewerkers op peil brengen en houden; - Innovaties toepassen (aanjagen en benutten), opgaven zo duurzaam mogelijk invullen; - In samenwerking op een duurzame en integrale manier de gladheidsbestrijding jaarlijks realiseren; - Het realiseren van de duurzaamheidsopgave: 50% minder CO2 uitstoot en 50% circulair handelen in 2030; - Het maken van de aanzet richting de duurzaamheidsopgave: volledig klimaatneutraal en circulair handelen in 2050.

description: Archaeological Processing and Archive Services for Accession and Storage in the National Museum of Ireland. The National Museum of Ireland requires archaeological processing services to; Sort, pack, document and prepare assemblages from a range of excavated or stored archaeological collections for storage/accession in the National Museum of Ireland to the contract specification and standards listed below. Contractors should demonstrate that they can provide a minimum of 1 supervisor archaeologist and 2 archaeological assistants (see definition and experience in Appendix A). A typical project of this type would have a minimum duration of at least 6 months. Sort, pack, document and transfer archaeological and other museum related archives, documents and reports in and/from a range of storage locations as outlined below. Contractors should demonstrate that they will be able to provide a minimum of 1 Archivist (see definition and experience in Appendix A). A typical work package could range from 6 months to a year. Provide services to wash, dry, process, pack and deliver osteological analysis and reporting to required standards (listed below) on assemblages of human remains of varying sizes including selection of samples for C14, Isotope and/or other analyses where recommended (varying sizes here could range from single bones to individual burials to large assemblages of articulated or disarticulated remains). A minimum requirement for a contract would be 1 Senior Osteoarchaeologist (see definition and experience in Appendix A) and the contractor should include an additional minimum of 2 Osteoarchaeologists for larger assemblages.

description: CLIN 0001: 140�150 Ton Industrial CNC Hydraulic Press Brake Quantity: 1 EA Pricing Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Item Description: The Contractor shall furnish and deliver one (1) new (not refurbished or prototype) Industrial CNC Hydraulic Press Brake meeting the following minimum salient characteristics: Tonnage Capacity: 140 to 150 Tons of hydraulic bending force. Bending Bed Length: Minimum 120 inches (10-foot) total usable working length. Cannot exceed 10-feet working width Clearance Between Side Frames: Minimum 100 inches internal clearance to accommodate standard sheet widths. Physical Footprint Envelope: Total assembled machine footprint shall not exceed 156 inches (13 feet) in width. Electrical / Motor Limits: Please state the Amperage, Voltage, and Motor HP to determine the electrical requirements. Frame & Weight: Minimum net machine weight of 14,000 lbs constructed from fully welded, stress-relieved structural steel. Control System: Integrated 2-Axis CNC Controller capable of storing a minimum of 40 unique programs with programmable back-gauge positioning and bend sequence angles. Tooling & Safety: Includes a standard Gooseneck punch, multi-V bottom die set with quick-release clamping, dual foot-pedal controls, and an ANSI/OSHA-compliant integrated optical light-curtain safety system. Trade Compliance: Must be manufactured in the United States, a DFARS Qualifying Country (DFARS 225.872-1), or a Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant country. CLIN 0002: Turnkey Logistics, Rigging, Commissioning, & Training Quantity: 1 Job (JB) Pricing Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Item Description: The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, specialized equipment, transportation, and rigging necessary to perform complete delivery, inside placement, mechanical setup, and operational verification of the equipment provided under CLIN 0001: Freight & Delivery (F.O.B. Offloading & Heavy Rigging: Provide certified heavy machinery riggers, skates, and forklift/crane equipment capable of safely offloading the ~14,000�16,000 lb machine, transporting it through facility doorways/bays, and placing it onto the designated workshop concrete slab without damaging facility infrastructure. Mechanical Leveling & Anchoring: Level the machine to manufacturer tolerances and anchor/secure the chassis to the concrete floor per standard engineering safety guidelines. (Note: Facility electrical wiring up to the disconnect box to be provided by the Government; final hookup coordination by Contractor). Hydraulic Fluid & Commissioning: Fill the hydraulic reservoir with appropriate industrial-grade hydraulic fluid, verify pump pressures, test emergency stop/light-curtain systems, and perform a live test bend on government-furnished material to verify 2-axis CNC repeatability. On-Site Operator Training: Provide a minimum of four (4) to eight (8) hours of comprehensive on-site operator training for up to four (4) government personnel, covering machine startup, CNC programming, tool changes, basic maintenance procedures, and safety protocols.

Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments. 2. Basis for Sole-Source Justification Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined: Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government�s urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters. Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments. Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program. The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements. 3. title: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology
description: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify commercial capabilities. The information sought herein is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the Government as a result of information submitted in response to the RFI. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI, or otherwise pay for any information submitted by respondents to this request. This notice is for market research purposes only and is not indicative of a full requirement. Any proposed items must meet or exceed the following specifications: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology Introduction & Objective The Government is conducting market research to identify commercially available, mature, and emerging technology solutions capable of enhancing the safety, accountability, and survivability of every Army Special Operations Forces (ARSOF) Soldier participating in Assessment, Selection, Qualification, and Professional Military Education (PME) courses. The Government seeks to understand industry capabilities, technical maturity, scalability, cost drivers, and risks associated with a wearable solution that provides real-time two-way communication, accurate location tracking, and continuous biometric monitoring viewable by cadre and safety personnel for safety management and risk mitigation. ARSOF training pipelines subject candidates to physically and mentally demanding conditions across varied terrain, climate, and duration. These conditions present inherent risks�including heat injury, cardiac events, dehydration, hypothermia, and physical incapacitation�that may occur outside the immediate observation of cadre. A technology-enabled safety monitoring capability is sought to enable early detection of physiological distress, rapid location of distressed personnel, and timely medical intervention. Technical Requirements & Capabilities To meet the requirements of this RFI, proposed systems should satisfy the following criteria. Respondents need not address every area but should clearly identify which capabilities they can provide. 1 Two-Way Communication Reliable two-way communication between wearer and cadre or safety personnel, allowing cadre to communicate with any selected user individually or the entire cohort simultaneously. Users may only communicate directly with cadre. Communication options include voice, data, or a combination of both. Wearer-initiated distress or man-down alert capability. Automated alerts sent to cadre when biometric thresholds are exceeded. Operation in degraded, denied, or no-infrastructure environments, such as mesh networks, satellite, or cellular fallback. 2 GPS / Location Services Near-real-time geolocation with desired accuracy of 10 meters or less and updates occurring every 30 seconds or less. Configurable and on-demand location updates. Geofencing with automated alerts when boundaries are departed. Reliable performance in GPS-degraded environments. Wearers must not be able to access location or time data from the device. Automated alerts at the control center when a unit remains stationary for preset periods as specified by cadre. 3 Biometric Monitoring Continuous monitoring of core body temperature, and heart rate at a minimum. Configurable, course-specific alert thresholds. Additional desirable parameters include respiration rate, hydration indicators, skin temperature, gate measurement, blood oxygen saturation (SpO?), and fall/impact detection. Monitoring equipment must not be constrictive, restrictive, or otherwise detracting from training. 4 Cadre Monitoring / Command Dashboard AI enabled to assess all data collected and provide warnings Centralized, simultaneous, real-time view of all monitored personnel (location, biometrics, alerts) Monitor 400+ devices per base station. Easy to use with minimal training. 24/7 Software Support for troubleshooting. Tiered alerting (visual/audible/push). Historical data logging and after-action analytics. 5 Hardware / Wearable Lightweight, low-profile design that does not restrict movement or blood flow for the wearer. Ruggedized construction with a target rating of IP67 or higher. Battery life sufficient for training events lasting over 24 hours, with rapid recharging capability. If reusable, must be easily sanitized. Must not interfere with other devices or wearers when in proximity. Waterproof up to 2 meters or greater. Audible distress beacon for rapid locating of wearers in crisis. 6 Cybersecurity & Data Approach to DoD RMF / Authority to Operate (ATO) per DoDI 8510.01. FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated encryption in transit and at rest. PHI/PII handling, role-based access, data ownership, and disposition. Information Requested from Industry- Interested vendors are requested to submit white papers or product data sheets, not to exceed 8 pages, detailing the following: Section A � Company Information 1. Company name, address, CAGE Code, UEI, and primary point of contact 2. Business size and socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code (e.g., small business, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone) 3. Commercial and/or government customer base relevant to this capability Section B � Solution / Capability Description 1. Description of your solution and which capability areas it addresses 2. Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and current maturity (fielded, prototype, in development) 3. Demonstrated performance in austere, disconnected, or military environments 4. Known limitations, constraints, or accuracy/reliability considerations Section C � Cybersecurity & Data 1. Current ATO status or RMF experience within DoD; estimated timeline to achieve ATO if not already held 2. Approach to protecting PHI/PII, encryption, and data ownership/disposition Section D � Implementation & Sustainment 1. Scalability to support large cohorts and multiple geographically dispersed locations 2. Training, technical support, maintenance, warranty, and sustainment approach 3. Lead times for delivery, fielding, and standup Section E � Current Contracts 1. Existing contract vehicles through which the solution is available (e.g., GSA Schedule, SEWP, CSO/OTA eligibility, SBIR/STTR) Section F � Optional 1. Any additional information, innovations, or recommendations relevant to this requirement 2. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost/pricing model (e.g., per-device, subscription, enterprise license) Documentation provided must address all required elements listed herein. Providing only a reference to a website is unacceptable for purposes of this announcement and will not be considered. All proprietary or corporate data received must be clearly identified. Do NOT submit classified material. Contractors interested in providing these supplies shall be registered in the System for Award Management (www.sam.gov). The Government makes no commitment to respond to questions submitted in response to this notice. No requests for capability briefings will be honored as a result of this notice. Information provided will not be used as a part of any subsequent solicitation requirement. No reimbursements will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and/or any follow-up information requests. Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated requests for quotations that may be issued. Respondents will NOT be individually notified of the results. However, if the final determination results in the verification of a sole-source negotiation, a Notice of Intent to Sole Source and the redacted Justification and Approval will be posted to www.sam.gov.

title: Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations Maritime Targeting Cell Systems
description: General Announcement THIS NOTICE OF INTENT/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY. Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments. 2. Basis for Sole-Source Justification Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined: Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government�s urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters. Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments. Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program. The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements. 3. Capability Statement Submission Instructions THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. However, all responsible sources may submit a technical capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's operational and technical requirements. The Government will not be responsible for any cost incurred in responding to this notice; however, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet the operational and technical requirements and past performance data no later than 12:00pm local time, Quantico, VA on 17 September 2026. Submissions received within 15 calendar days of this publication will be considered by the Government. Information received will be evaluated solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All submissions shall become Government property and will not be returned. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 7F20, IT and Telecom � IT Management Tool/Products (Hardware and Perpetual License Software). The contractor or site owner shall provide land use, access, infrastructure, and utilities necessary to support BLM-owned communications equipment and ensure uninterrupted radio communications services critical to employee safety and mission operations. Sole Source Contract Announcement This notice informs the public of BLM�s intent to award a sole source contract to provide land use, access, infrastructure and utilities necessary to support BLM-owned communications equipment and ensure uninterrupted radio communications services critical to employee safety and mission operations. The contract will be awarded in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 5.301(b)/5.101(b)(i) and will utilize Simplified Acquisition Procedures as authorized by RFO 6.103-1(b) under 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). This statute authorizes sole source procurement when the property or services required are available only from one responsible source, or from a limited number of responsible sources, and no other type of property or services will satisfy the agency�s needs. No alternative sites in the vicinity meet the operational requirements due to the terrain and elevation of Snow Peak which provide critical connectivity. The existing infrastructure investments at this site would be cost-prohibitive to replicate elsewhere. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Yole Inc
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if it's determined only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements, as supplemented with additional information in this notice. The U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), Shared Services Procurement Office (SSPO), located in Washington, D.C., intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis and award a contract to Yole Inc. on behalf of the International Trade Administration (ITA), Office of Industry & Analysis (I&A). This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of permitting other than full and open competition in accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 12.102 and in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901. This acquisition will result in a purchase order with a base 12-month period and one 12-month option period. DOC plans to issue a sole source purchase order to Yole for the acquisition of market intelligence reports covering key segments of the semiconductor and information and communications technology (ICT) industries. I&A requires specialized market intelligence to support OICT's responsibility to provide senior Department of Commerce officials, U.S. Government agencies, and U.S. firms with data, analyses, and recommendations concerning market trends within the semiconductor and ICT sectors. The required market intelligence supports OICT's analysis of technology trends, company market shares, global supply chains, U.S. industry competitiveness, export markets, and the development of effective trade policy. Yole Inc. is uniquely qualified to satisfy this requirement because the Government's requirement is for specifically identified proprietary Yole Group market intelligence publications and associated access to the Yole Group analysts responsible for the underlying research and analysis. The required reports are Yole Group products addressing specialized semiconductor markets, technologies, supply chains, and industry developments. As the publisher and owner of these proprietary market intelligence products, Yole controls the content, underlying research, methodologies, analyses, and associated analyst expertise incorporated into the required publications. The requirement cannot be satisfied merely through the acquisition of generalized semiconductors or ICT market research from another market research provider. OICT requires the specific Yole Group reports identified in the PWS, as well as direct consultation with relevant Yole Group analysts to clarify and provide context regarding the information contained in those reports. Other market research companies may offer research concerning similar industries or technologies; however, those products would contain independently developed datasets, methodologies, forecasts, market segmentation, and analyses and would therefore not provide the specific Yole research products required by OICT. Accordingly, Yole Inc. is the only source reasonably capable of providing the specific proprietary publications and associated Yole analyst consultations required to meet the Government's stated need. Award to another source would not provide the Government with the required Yole Group research and analyst access. Therefore, use of the sole-source authority provided by RFO 12.102 is appropriate for this acquisition. As previously stated, this is NOT a solicitation for quotations, quotation abstracts, a request for competitive quotations; or request for competitive proposals; There is no solicitation package available for review due to the Government�s intention to conduct this requirement as a sole source award. If a company determines that their company can meet all requirements mentioned above, the company shall submit a written response within 15 days from the date of publication of this synopsis for it to be taken into consideration by the Government. Responses must clearly and thoroughly defend any claims or assertions that attempt to refute the Government�s claim. A determination by the Government not to proceed with this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely with the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Information received on this notice must eliminate the Government's concerns and address how the required services can be provided. If no qualified/affirmative responses are received within 15 days of this notice to determine whether a qualified source is more advantageous to the Government, a contract will be awarded to Yole Inc. Any questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to Jameka Anderson (JAnderson1@doc.gov). Telephonic questions or requests will not be considered.

title: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology
description: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify commercial capabilities. The information sought herein is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the Government as a result of information submitted in response to the RFI. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI, or otherwise pay for any information submitted by respondents to this request. This notice is for market research purposes only and is not indicative of a full requirement. Any proposed items must meet or exceed the following specifications: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology Introduction & Objective The Government is conducting market research to identify commercially available, mature, and emerging technology solutions capable of enhancing the safety, accountability, and survivability of every Army Special Operations Forces (ARSOF) Soldier participating in Assessment, Selection, Qualification, and Professional Military Education (PME) courses. The Government seeks to understand industry capabilities, technical maturity, scalability, cost drivers, and risks associated with a wearable solution that provides real-time two-way communication, accurate location tracking, and continuous biometric monitoring viewable by cadre and safety personnel for safety management and risk mitigation. ARSOF training pipelines subject candidates to physically and mentally demanding conditions across varied terrain, climate, and duration. These conditions present inherent risks�including heat injury, cardiac events, dehydration, hypothermia, and physical incapacitation�that may occur outside the immediate observation of cadre. A technology-enabled safety monitoring capability is sought to enable early detection of physiological distress, rapid location of distressed personnel, and timely medical intervention. Technical Requirements & Capabilities To meet the requirements of this RFI, proposed systems should satisfy the following criteria. Respondents need not address every area but should clearly identify which capabilities they can provide. 1 Two-Way Communication Reliable two-way communication between wearer and cadre or safety personnel, allowing cadre to communicate with any selected user individually or the entire cohort simultaneously. Users may only communicate directly with cadre. Communication options include voice, data, or a combination of both. Wearer-initiated distress or man-down alert capability. Automated alerts sent to cadre when biometric thresholds are exceeded. Operation in degraded, denied, or no-infrastructure environments, such as mesh networks, satellite, or cellular fallback. 2 GPS / Location Services Near-real-time geolocation with desired accuracy of 10 meters or less and updates occurring every 30 seconds or less. Configurable and on-demand location updates. Geofencing with automated alerts when boundaries are departed. Reliable performance in GPS-degraded environments. Wearers must not be able to access location or time data from the device. Automated alerts at the control center when a unit remains stationary for preset periods as specified by cadre. 3 Biometric Monitoring Continuous monitoring of core body temperature, and heart rate at a minimum. Configurable, course-specific alert thresholds. Additional desirable parameters include respiration rate, hydration indicators, skin temperature, gate measurement, blood oxygen saturation (SpO?), and fall/impact detection. Monitoring equipment must not be constrictive, restrictive, or otherwise detracting from training. 4 Cadre Monitoring / Command Dashboard AI enabled to assess all data collected and provide warnings Centralized, simultaneous, real-time view of all monitored personnel (location, biometrics, alerts) Monitor 400+ devices per base station. Easy to use with minimal training. 24/7 Software Support for troubleshooting. Tiered alerting (visual/audible/push). Historical data logging and after-action analytics. 5 Hardware / Wearable Lightweight, low-profile design that does not restrict movement or blood flow for the wearer. Ruggedized construction with a target rating of IP67 or higher. Battery life sufficient for training events lasting over 24 hours, with rapid recharging capability. If reusable, must be easily sanitized. Must not interfere with other devices or wearers when in proximity. Waterproof up to 2 meters or greater. Audible distress beacon for rapid locating of wearers in crisis. 6 Cybersecurity & Data Approach to DoD RMF / Authority to Operate (ATO) per DoDI 8510.01. FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated encryption in transit and at rest. PHI/PII handling, role-based access, data ownership, and disposition. title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation System - Indianapolis VAMC
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, �Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services,� as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation RFQ- 36C25026Q1013 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026. This is a firm fixed price, Small Business Set-Aside solicitation. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) number is 334510. NOTE: This solicitation is for one Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation System that is FDA-cleared for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). All interested companies shall provide quotations for the requirements listed below. Materials and parts will be delivered to: Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center, 1481 W. 10th St., Indianapolis, IN 46202, FOB destination. Minimum Requirements The required TMS device must have the following salient characteristics, specific to the clinical needs and operation at our VAMC: - Delivers a series of pulsed magnetic stimuli to targeted regions of the brain, following predefined treatment protocols. - Non-invasive procedure�requires no anesthesia and does not disrupt normal cognitive functions. - Flat purchase model: No pay-per-use fees; acquisition includes all treatment protocols. - Upgradeable treatment protocols: Device must support future protocol updates. - High patient throughput: Utilizes a liquid-cooled TMS coil for sustained clinical use with minimal downtime. - Low acoustic noise: Device operates at low intensity acoustic signature (clicking), minimizing patient discomfort. - System adaptable to any practice size: Must be installable in a variety of clinical settings. - Theraburst stimulation capability as an available therapy option. - Clinical safety and efficacy: Free from common antidepressant side effects (weight gain, sexual dysfunction). - Onsite installation and training: Contractor provides initial setup and hands-on orientation for clinical staff. - Ongoing technical and marketing support included. - Comprehensive documentation and warranty: Delivered with product documentation, warranty information, and support contacts. TMS device is being used to treat: - Major Depressive Disorder (MDD): Specifically for patients who have not responded to at least one antidepressant medication. - Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD): FDA-cleared protocols for OCD treatment are also utilized. The goal is to provide safe, evidence-based neurostimulation for refractory depression and OCD, improving patient outcomes where conventional pharmacologic treatments have failed or are not tolerated. Contact: Rachel MacRae, Contracting Specialist, via email at rachel.macrae@va.gov. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. Only written inquiries received directly for the offeror are acceptable. All quotes must be received by 9/17/2026 by 12:00pm EST to Rachel MacRae (rachel.macrae@va.gov). An award will be based upon a comparative evaluation of quotes in accordance with the Simplified Acquisition Procedures of RFO FAR 12. Comparative evaluation is the side by side pairwise comparison of quotes based on factors resulting in a Contracting Officer decision for the quote most favorable to the Government. The following must be completed to be considered for award: - Quote with the following information o The solicitation number; o The name, address, telephone number of the Offeror; o The Offeror�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and, if applicable, Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) indicator;o A technical description of the items being offered in sufficient detail to evaluate compliance with the requirements in the solicitation. This may include product literature, or other documents, if necessary; - FAR 52.225-2 � Buy American Certificate (see attached) - Offerors must complete annual representations and certifications electronically via the System for Award Management (SAM) website located at https://sam.gov. - To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: �The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition.� OR �The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" Quoters shall list exception(s) and rationale for the exception(s), if any. Contractor shall provide an authorized distribution letter. All warranty and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions. title: Intent to Sole Source Service Agreement for Hamilton Equipment
description: This is notice of intent to award to Hamilton Company (UEI: LD1MPMMCBWJ9) for one?year Premium Plus Service Agreement for Hamilton NGS MOA STAR Workstation, SN AB03. In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.102 (a), the following documents the decision to restrict competition for this acquisition. Mission Area and Contracting Activity. Requesting Activity Agency: USDA APHIS PPQ S&T Plant Pathogen Confirmatory Diagnostics Laboratory (PPCDL) 9901 Powder Mill Rd. Laurel, MD 20708 Contracting Activity: USDA, APHIS, MRPBS, AAMD Office of Contracting and Procurement 250 Marquette Ave Ste 410, Minneapolis, MN 55401 Brief Description of Supplies or Services This procurement is for the purchase of a one?year Premium Plus Service Agreement for Hamilton NGS MOA STAR Workstation, SN AB03. The Hamilton NGS MOA STAR Workstation is a critical component of Plant Pathogen Confirmatory Diagnostics Laboratory (PPCDL)�s molecular diagnostic workflows. It integrates standardized hardware, software, and method programming, and offers the largest repertoire of biologically validated methods for streamlined setup and implementation. This instrument directly supports PPCDL�s confirmatory diagnostics mission. Ensuring the workstation is maintained in optimal operating condition is essential to preserving the reliability and integrity of PPCDL operations. Premium Plus Service Agreement Includes: Priority dispatch for contract customers A target response time of 24 hours for a down instrument A guaranteed response time of 48 hours for a down instrument A guaranteed call back time of 4 hours Parts, travel, and labor costs The agreement will include one PM and one verification services. Justification for Restricting Competition and the Basis for that Decision. A. Explain the unique qualifications/characteristics of the proposed contractor or product and why no other contractor or product/service can meet the Government's need. PPCDL operates under the ISO/IEC 17025 standard, which requires that all equipment maintenance and calibration services be performed either by the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or by an ISO?accredited service provider. Non?compliance with this requirement would jeopardize PPCDL�s accreditation status and impair the laboratory�s ability to carry out its federally mandated confirmatory diagnostic responsibilities. Hamilton is the manufacturer of the Hamilton NGS MOA STAR Workstation and the sole provider of the instrument�s proprietary software and firmware. Servicing the workstation through third?party vendors would present significant risks, as those vendors may not have access to the Hamilton?specific factory software required to reset internal calibrations or perform essential firmware updates. In addition, third?party providers often lack access to genuine Hamilton replacement components, such as O?rings, stop disks, and channels, and may rely on aftermarket or harvested parts, which could compromise instrument performance and reliability. For these reasons, Hamilton is the only service provider capable of meeting the technical, compliance, and quality requirements necessary to maintain the instrument under ISO/IEC 17025. B. Describe market research conducted and the results or the reason why no market research was conducted. Market research was not conducted because the instrument requires manufacturer?specific software, calibration tools, and proprietary components that are available exclusively through Hamilton. Third?party vendors do not have access to the Hamilton factory firmware, calibration utilities, or genuine replacement parts. Maintaining compliance with ISO/IEC 17025 also requires that all service and calibration activities be performed by the original equipment manufacturer or an ISO?accredited provider with OEM authorization. Because Hamilton is the sole qualified provider, additional market research was unnecessary.

title: K-12 Newcomer Curriculum and Customization Services for ORR
description: Amendment 1: The purpose of this amendment is to: Extend the response due date to September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET); and Invite industry representatives to participate in a roundtable discussion with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) to further discuss the requirement and provide industry feedback. Information regarding the roundtable discussion, including registration instructions, is provided in the PowerPoint presentation located in the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Objective: The Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) is conducting market research to identify qualified contractors capable of providing a commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) K-12 educational curriculum tailored for newcomer and migrant students, along with professional services to customize the material to fit specific regional, demographic, and compliance requirements. The curriculum model should include child assessments (initial assessment, assessment every 30 days, and an exit assessment). The curriculum model shall be trauma informed and integrate social emotional learning; and be customizable to the different ORR funded residential care programs such as shelters, secure care, long-term foster care, therapeutic care sites, and a potential home-schooling model. Background and Target Population: The target student population consist of K-12 newcomers, immigrant children, and migrant youth. These students often present unique educational needs including: Varying levels of English Language Proficiency (ELP), including students with Interrupted Formal Education (SIFE). A critical need for rapid acculturation, social-emotional learning (SEL) support, foundational literacy/numeracy, including trauma informed teaching strategies and guidance. Highly transient lifestyles requiring flexible, modular learning units. Scope of Work: The selected contractor shall deliver a comprehensive solution consisting of both curriculum materials and instructional design customization services; including professional services contractors to support ORR headquarters with successful implementation and monitoring of K-12 curriculum for newcomers in all ORR funded residential and care programs for unaccompanied alien children (UAC), as well as providing ORR funded program teaching staff with training and technical assistance. It shall include child assessments (initial assessment, assessment every 30 days, and an exit assessment), and be trauma informed and integrate social emotional learning.

title: Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations Maritime Targeting Cell Systems
description: General Announcement THIS NOTICE OF INTENT/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY. Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments. Basis for Sole-Source Justification Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined: Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government�s urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters. Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments. Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program. The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements. Capability Statement Submission Instructions THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. However, all responsible sources may submit a technical capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's operational and technical requirements. The Government will not be responsible for any cost incurred in responding to this notice; however, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet the operational and technical requirements and past performance data no later than 12:00pm local time, Quantico, VA on 17 September 2026. Submissions received within 15 calendar days of this publication will be considered by the Government. All submissions shall become Government property and will not be returned. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract - Parking Garage Services
description: 1. Action Description The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) intends to award a sole-source firm-fixed-price contract to Arlington VA I FGF LLC, Chicago IL, the owner and lessor of the property located at 675 N. Randolph Street in Arlington, Virginia, to provide secure, controlled parking and related facility support services for the below-grade structed parking garage directly beneath DARPA Headquarters. 2. Background and Scope of Services DARPA requires continued control of the below-grade structured parking garage located at 675 N. Randolph Street. The garage is physically integrated with and located directly beneath the DARPA Headquarters facility. The Contractor will be required to provide comprehensive facility support services necessary to maintain the garage in a safe, operational, and secure condition. These services may include structural maintenance; mechanical, ventilation, and related building system support; fire and life-safety system support; emergency infrastructure support; compliance with Department of War below-grade, structured parking garage at 675 North Randolph Street, Arlington, VA, to ensure a fully secure and operational exclusive-use parking facility for DARPA. Historically, parking and associated access-control capabilities were included within the master building lease managed by Washington Headquarters Services (WHS). As a result of changes to the WHS leasing structure, these requirements will no longer be included in the master lease. Therefore, DARPA intends to independently procure the services necessary to maintain control of the below-grade parking area and support the physical-security requirements of its headquarters facility. 3. Authority and Basis for the Proposed Sole Source Acquisition This proposed acquisition is being conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. � 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements." DARPA�s market research identified numerous commercial parking facilities in Arlington, Virginia that can provide general commercial parking. However, the Government has not identified an alternative facility capable of satisfying all of the following requirements: Unique Physical Location and Integration. The required parking facility is physically integrated with and located directly beneath DARPA Headquarters at 675 N. Randolph Street. No other commercial parking facility can provide the same physical relationship to the DARPA facility. Physical Security and Access Control. DARPA requires controlled vehicle access to the below-grade parking area to support the physical security requirements applicable to the Agency headquarters facility. For instance, in accordance with Department of Defense (currently Department of War (DoW)) Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-010-01 (DoD Minimum Antiterrorism Standards for Buildings), access control to subterranean structures directly beneath DoW offices is a critical security vulnerability. Proprietary Rights and Building Systems. The Government requires access to the garage and the building systems integral to its operation, including structural, ventilation, mechanical, and fire and life safety systems that support the garage. Arlington VA I FGF, LLC owns and controls the property where the garage facility is located. Because those rights and systems are controlled by the property owner, another source could not independently provide the Government with exclusive rights to the same facility without authorization from the owner. Continuity of Operations. DARPA requires a transition that does not create an interruption in the physical security and access control measures supporting DARPA Headquarters. 4. Determination DARPA has determined that Arlington VA I FGF, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services, and no other type of services will satisfy all the Agency�s requirements because: The Government�s requirement extends beyond obtaining parking spaces in the Arlington, Virgina area. An alternative, off-site parking facility would not provide the Government with control of the area directly beneath DARPA Headquarters or eliminate the Government�s continuing requirement to maintain appropriate physical security controls over that area. Unrestricted or uncontrolled commercial use of the area directly beneath the headquarters could adversely affect the physical-security posture of the facility. Maintaining the existing below-grade parking facility avoids the operational and security disruption that could result from attempting to relocate the parking function while simultaneously maintaining control of the area directly beneath the headquarters. 5. Notice to Interested Sources This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. It is issued to determine whether any responsible sources can demonstrate their capability to satisfy the Government�s complete requirement and provide a basis for the Government to reconsider the contemplated sole-source acquisition. Interested sources are invited to submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstration, with objective and specific information, their ability to satisfy all of the Government�s requirements. The ability to provide ordinary commercial parking spaces at another Arlington, Virginia location, standing alone, will not satisfy the requirement. A response should address, at a minimum, the following: Physical and Legal Access. Legal authority and practical ability to obtain the rights necessary to provide exclusive and controlled use of, and perform the required services within, the below-grade parking facility directly beneath 675 North Randolph Street in Arlington, Virginia. Security and Access Control. Ability to satisfy the Government�s physical security and controlled access requirements applicable to the below-grade parking facility, including applicable Department of War requirements, such as compliance with DoD Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-010-01 for subterranean facility access control. Continuity of Operations. Ability to provide uninterrupted services during transition and throughout contract performance without compromising DARPA�s physical security requirements. Organizational Capability. Identify relevant experience, technical capabilities, facilities, personnel, and other resources demonstrating ability to perform the required services. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration. Provide documentation of current registration in SAM, including a valid Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE code, as applicable. Interested sources should submit a capability statement addressing the requirements identified above to the Primary and Secondary points of contact listed above no later than the Response Deadline. Generic statements of interest or statements that merely demonstrate an ability to provide commercial parking services will not be sufficient. The Government will consider all timely and substantive responses solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the contemplated contract action, based on responses to this notice or otherwise, will be within the Government�s discretion and consistent with applicable acquisition laws and regulations. The Government is not responsible for costs incurred by interested sources in preparing or submitting responses to this notice.

The contractor shall furnish all equipment, materials, labor, supervision, and quality control to perform work for VA Project 635-21-139 Repair Parking Garage 1 Deficiencies located East of the VA Medical Center main building at the corner of NE 13th street and N. Kelly Avenue, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma 73104. SCOPE OF WORK: This summary is not intended to be all inclusive and does not absolve the contractor of responsibility to address the defects and deficiencies of the Parking Garage 1 consistent with the contents of the specs and/or drawings. Bidders are responsible for the entirety of the project scope described in the contract documents (drawings and specifications) and shall submit RFI s on any conflicts between drawings and specifications immediately that may impact bids. Bidders are responsible for all work specified or shown in the bid documents including the Statement of Work, Drawings, and Specifications. Work includes but is not limited to the following: Parking striping and signage, fixing a sidewalk that is not ADA compliant, installing suicide prevention, providing a new stairwell on the south side of the parking garage. Civil, architectural, electrical, lighting, wayfinding, low voltage, and structural systems are included in this project. The contractor shall comply with all requirements listed in the project solicitation including the construction drawings, the project specifications, and all solicitation amendments as may be issued. These documents will be followed during construction and shall be considered project requirements. The areas adjacent to the proposed addition shall be continuously occupied by the OKC VAMC. The Contractor shall implement phasing to ensure that the construction will not impact or impede the VAMC s mission to care for the Veterans. The contractor shall provide quality control of all work conducted and the individual appointed shall be competent and educated/experienced in the field of work this scope encompasses. Codes and Standards: The Contractor shall follow all applicable codes and standards to this type of work including but not limited to Health Care System Memorandums (HCSM), OSHA Guidelines, NFPA 101, NFPA 70, Lock-out-Tag-out, and Rules of Station. title: 52000QR260027907- CGC Northland- Vane Axial Ventilation Fan Rebuild and Reconditioning
description: Solicitation Amendment #1 The purpose of this amendment is to resolve a discrepancy in the original solicitation notice regarding the SOW technical specifications and to formally extend the quotation submission deadline. The Government is amending the solicitation to clarify the submission requirements and ensure all potential offerors are quoting against the correct technical parameters. Summary of Changes: Equipment Baseline Correction: The original SOW contained conflicting baseline specifications regarding the fan motor horsepower and low-speed operational thresholds. Based on detailed technical verification, the following corrections have been made: The SOW has been updated to reflect the correct 10HP motor requirement (superseding the previously noted 2.5HP reference). The low-speed operating parameter has been corrected to 1150 RPM (superseding the previously noted 846 RPM reference). Addition of Coating (Painting) Specifications: The original solicitation did not include specific technical guidelines for protective coatings. A paint specification has been added to the SOW detailing the required surface preparation, primer, and topcoat standards. To accommodate these updates, the original Statement of Work is hereby removed and replaced in its entirety with the updated SOW. Instructions to Offerors: All other terms and conditions of the original solicitation remain unchanged. If a proposal has already been submitted and no response or revised proposal is received from the bidder on this amendment, the original proposal will be deemed final and binding and evaluated as-is. It is the sole responsibility of the interested party to monitor the solicitation for all modifications. The new closing date for this solicitation is extended to Thursday, 17 September 2026, 1:00PM EST. Proposals must be received by this deadline to be considered. title: IEE Sources Sought � 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services � Great Plains Area.
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (GPA IHS) Sources Sought Notice Number: IHS1526971 NOTICE TYPE AND PURPOSE This is a Sources Sought Notice for market research purposes only. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). No contract will be awarded as a result of this announcement. The Indian Health Service (IHS) is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs), Small Businesses, 8(a) participants, HUBZone Small Businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs), and Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSBs) capable of performing the requirement described herein prior to issuance of a potential solicitation. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this notice. Responses shall be submitted by email. No presentations will be scheduled. Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether a set-aside is appropriate. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561320, Temporary Help Services. Respondents may identify other NAICS codes they believe are more appropriate to the requirement, such as those applicable to offices of physicians or mental health specialists. 1.0 BACKGROUND The Great Plains Area Office (GPAO) works in conjunction with its 19 Indian Health Service Units and Tribal Managed Service Units to provide health care to approximately 122,000 Native Americans located in North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Iowa. The Area Office�s service units include seven hospitals, eight health centers, and several smaller health stations and satellite clinics. IHS anticipates providing 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year (24/7/365) synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health services in support of Emergency Department (ED) operations at facilities within the Great Plains Area. 2.0 OBJECTIVE The mission of the Indian Health Service is to raise the physical, mental, social, and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. As part of this mission, IHS is committed to ensuring the safety and security of its patients, staff, and facilities while providing high-quality health care services across its regions. The purpose of this requirement is to provide services to patients presenting to Emergency Departments with suicide attempts, acute psychiatric crises, substance-related emergencies, and co-occurring disorders. Timely behavioral health assessment and intervention are critical to patient safety, regulatory compliance, and appropriate disposition. 3.0 SCOPE The Contractor shall provide qualified, licensed independent behavioral health clinicians, including psychologists, psychiatrists, Licensed Clinical Social Workers (LCSWs), Licensed Professional Counselors-Mental Health (LPC-MHs), or equivalent professionals, to deliver real-time telebehavioral health services. Services shall include, as clinically indicated and/or required by facility workflows: Suicide risk assessment and completion of the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) with Suicide Assessment Five-Step Evaluation and Triage (SAFE-T) for patients presenting with suicidal ideation or suicide attempts. Crisis intervention, de-escalation guidance, and reassessment as indicated. Individualized Stanley-Brown Safety Planning, including lethal means counseling when appropriate. Placement coordination for patients requiring higher levels of care, including inpatient psychiatric care, crisis stabilization, and detoxification services, with documentation of placement attempts. Language-access coordination, including telephonic, video remote interpreting (VRI), and American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter services available within 15 minutes of request and documented in the Electronic Health Record (EHR). Culturally responsive and trauma-informed care, supported by annual clinician training in areas such as cultural competency, implicit bias, and trauma-informed care. For patients presenting with acute psychiatric crises, qualified prescribing providers�including psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, or psychologists with prescribing privileges�shall be available to consult with the ED provider regarding appropriate medication stabilization. Prior to initiation of a consultation, the Contractor shall receive a report from the referring provider or designee. At the conclusion of the patient evaluation, the telebehavioral health provider shall provide a report to the referring provider or designee. 4.0 CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS AND PERSONNEL QUALIFICATIONS The Contractor shall maintain sufficient qualified personnel and operational capacity to provide the required synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health coverage 24/7/365, including weekends and Federal holidays. Personnel shall possess the professional qualifications, licensure, credentials, and prescribing authority, as applicable, necessary to perform the services described in this notice. 5.0 TYPE OF ORDER The anticipated award is a firm-fixed-price, performance-based acquisition purchase order. 6.0 ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance is a Base Period plus Four Option Years, as follows: Base Period: August 1, 2027 � July 31, 2028 Option Year 1: August 1, 2028 � July 31, 2029 Option Year 2: August 1, 2029 � July 31, 2030 Option Year 3: August 1, 2030 � July 31, 2031 Option Year 4: August 1, 2031 � July 31, 2032 7.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE The requirement supports facilities within the Great Plains Area, Indian Health Service. The initial scope includes the following Emergency Departments: Pine Ridge Hospital � Pine Ridge, South Dakota Rosebud Hospital � Rosebud, South Dakota Eagle Butte Hospital � Eagle Butte, South Dakota Fort Yates Hospital � Fort Yates, North Dakota Belcourt Hospital � Belcourt, North Dakota 8.0 REPORTS, DELIVERABLES, AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE The Contractor shall provide synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health services 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, including weekends and Federal holidays, unless otherwise specified in an applicable order. Services shall be provided utilizing Webex or another platform identified by the Indian Health Service. 9.0 PAYMENT AND INVOICING Invoices submitted under any resulting award shall be processed through the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) in accordance with HHSAR 352.232-71, Electronic Submission and Processing of Payment Requests. Payment will be made upon receipt of a complete and accurate invoice and successful completion of acceptance in accordance with the Prompt Payment Act. Invoices shall contain all required information and supporting documentation and shall be submitted through IPP.gov, with a copy provided to Dustin Appl, COR I, or his designee. Invoice Frequency and Submission Invoices shall be submitted in accordance with the terms of any resulting award and shall reference the applicable contract or order number. 10.0 CAPABILITY STATEMENT / INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties are expected to review this notice and the associated Performance Work Statement (PWS), if provided with the notice, to familiarize themselves with the requirements. Failure to do so is at the respondent�s own risk. Capability statements shall include the following: Company Name. Company Information: Point of contact, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and website address. Authorized Point of Contact: Name, telephone number, and email address of a company representative with the authority and knowledge necessary to clarify the company�s response with Government representatives. title: FY 26 - FY 31 Unaccompanied Housing Wi-Fi
description: 14th Contracting Squadron located at Columbus AFB, MS 39710, intends to award a sole source award to Cable One INC/ dba Spraklight, 606 Noble Street, Anniston, Alabama 36201. This requirement is for a turnkey solution to engineer, furnish, install, test, and maintain a commercial wireless internet (Wi-Fi) service for the unaccompanied housing dormitories and designated common areas at Columbus Air Force Base (CAFB), MS. The objective is to deliver reliable, high-speed Internet access to all residents at no cost to them, in compliance with all Department of the Air Force policies. The purpose of this service is to provide Dorm Wireless Internet to 3-day rooms, 94 dorm rooms, and 3 outdoor pavilions postured on one campus at Columbus Air Force Base (AFB). The contractor shall provide installation and all necessary equipment, to include up to 73 modems, up to two WI-FI repeaters and up to seven 24 port switches as specified in the Statement of Work (SOW) for a period of five years one (1) Base Year of 12 months and four (4) 12-month option years. Additionally, for Wide Area WorkFlow (WAWF) invoicing, the BPN for both the Inspector and the Acceptor is F1N3BA; no separate inspector is necessary. The Government intends to acquire this commercial service under FAR Part 12 and to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 and DFARS 206.302-1. The proposed source is Cable One INC/ dba Spraklight . Based on the facts documented in the justification, only this source can meet the Government�s requirement because Sparklight (Cable One, Inc.) is currently the only internet service provider with existing cable infrastructure on Columbus Air Force Base capable of providing the required dormitory wireless internet service to the UEQ campus. Other potential carriers do not currently have the necessary on-site infrastructure and equipment and have not obtained the installation franchise agreement required to provide internet service on the installation. This is not a request for competitive proposals, quotations, or offers. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation that will be considered by the Government. Interested sources shall demonstrate their capability to provide a turnkey dormitory Wi-Fi solution that meets the Government�s requirements, including engineering, furnishing, installation, testing, sustainment, continuity of resident service, interoperability with existing infrastructure as applicable, licensing, and all other requirements identified in the attached public-release SOW/PWS. The Government will evaluate timely responses to determine whether another source can meet the requirement and whether a competitive procurement is warranted. Responses must contain sufficient detail for the Government to assess the source�s technical capability and transition approach. Submit responses through the contact method identified in the SAM.gov notice no later than the stated response deadline. Capability statements and related materials must be e-mailed to Brownlee, John M at john.brownlee.2@us.af.mil and Booth, Dylan L at dylan.booth.1@us.af.mil by 12:00 PM Central Daylight Time on 17th September 2026.
