title: FORT RILEY - CHAPEL AUDIO VISUAL EQUIPMENT UPGRADE
description: This requirement encompasses the commercial procurement, delivery, physical installation, and system-wide integration of upgraded Audio-Visual (AV) components across Kapaun Chapel, St. Mary's Chapel, and Morris Hill Chapel at Fort Riley, Kansas. The scope of work requires furnishing and integrating digital audio mixing consoles (Yamaha TF1 or functionally equivalent systems featuring motorized faders, multi-scene recall, and native Dante audio network compatibility), commercial power amplifiers, and wireless microphone systems with existing sanctuary acoustic infrastructure. In Kapaun Chapel, the contractor shall install a high-output solid-state laser projection system delivering a minimum of 9,000 ANSI lumens at native WUXGA (1920x1200) resolution with an operational lifespan of at least 20,000 maintenance-free hours, supported by HDBaseT or equivalent signal extension systems capable of transmitting uncompressed 4K UHD video up to 330 feet (100 meters). Ancillary services include the safe de-installation and relocation of one government-owned Yamaha TF3 mixing console from St. Mary's Chapel to Morris Hill Chapel, the supply of specialized AV equipment housing/furniture, and the routing of new plenum-rated, structured, and labeled cabling through existing sanctuary conduits. Final contract closeout requires professional acoustic system calibration, delivery of comprehensive as-built line schematics, complete handover of all uncompiled editable control programming files and administrative passwords to prevent proprietary lock-in, and a minimum of four hours of on-site operational user training for government personnel. A site visit will be held on 10 September 2026 @ 1400 hrs CDT at Kapaun Chapel, then at St. Mary's Chapel. Questions are due no later than 14 September 2026 @ 1000 hrs CDT. Any questions received after the deadline will not receive a response.

title: Intent to Award - Monaco Enterprise, Inc.
description: Eglin Air Force Base, FL intends to award a Single Source, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract as authorized by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(b) to Monaco Enterprises, Inc, 14820 East Sprague Ave, Spokane Valley, WA 99216 The Monaco Enterprise system serves as the primary infrastructure for the installation's Fire Alarm Reporting and Mass Notification System (MNS). Continuous, reliable operation of the Monaco system is required to meet National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) and Department of War (DoW) life safety regulations, ensuring rapid response to fire, medical, and security emergencies. Furthermore, DoW mandates that all Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT) systems run on supported operating systems to comply with current Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs). With previous Windows OS versions reaching EOL, upgrading to Windows 11 is a non-negotiable requirement to maintain a secure cybersecurity posture and retain the system's Authority to Operate (ATO). Failure to secure and execute this technology update will result in severe, cascading mission impacts across multiple domains. For Cybersecurity & Compliance, this means revocation of the system's Authority to Operate (ATO); the Authorizing Official (AO) will be forced to quarantine the Monaco system from the DoW Information Network to prevent lateral vulnerabilities. Market Research Assessment determined that Monaco Enterprises, Inc. is the best acquisition path and will be of the largest benefit to the Government. Pursuant to RFO 12.102(b) the Contracting Officer has determined that circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available. title: S--INDU Septic & Lift Station Pumping
description: Septic & Lift Station Pumping and Cleaning at Indiana Dunes National Park, Porter, Indiana The purpose of this amendment is to provide the date and time for a requested site visit and questions and answers asked thus far. The Site Visit is scheduled for 9/15/2026 at 11:00 AM CDT. Meeting location: HQ building, 1100 N Mineral Springs Rd Porter, IN. Meet at the flagpole. 1. Pricing basis. Attachment 3 requests one "EA" unit price per CLIN for routine, incident, and emergency pumping, while Attachment 2 lists tanks from 1,000 to 4,000 gallons. Will the Government evaluate price using the estimated quantities in Attachment 2? May quoters price by tank-size tier or per gallon, or is a single blended per-event price expected regardless of tank size? Answer: Quotes should show prices per gallon since the various tanks have different capacities. Incident and emergency prices should equal your per gallon price for those services plus whatever urgent service fees may be associated with each. You may use your own quote spreadsheet if that makes it easier. 2. Lift stations. The CLIN titles read "Septic & Lift Station Pumping," but the Statement of Work (Items 2 and 3) describes septic tank pumping and pipe cleaning. How many lift stations are included, and at what expected frequency? Answer: There are sixteen lift stations. One should be pumped once a year, and the rest only require service �as needed�. 3. Heavy cleaning. Please define "Heavy Cleaning" (CLINs 0007-0009) as distinct from routine pipe cleaning and confirm the unit basis for those CLINs (per event, per hour, or other). Answer: Routine cleaning being material removable by standard hydraulic jetting, while heavy cleaning would require multiple passes, mechanical cutting/descaling, specialized tooling, or debris removal beyond normal jetting. 4. State permits. SOW Item 2 states the contractor shall maintain all required state waste management and septic certifications, and the Technical Questionnaire contemplates subcontractors. Please confirm that the IDEM septage hauler registration and related permits may be held by the subcontractor that performs the pumping, with the prime responsible for compliance. Answer: That arrangement is acceptable. 5. Site visit. Attachment 1 (SOW) urges a site visit. Is one scheduled, or may quoters arrange one through the COR? Answer: Site Visit is scheduled for 9/15/2026 at 11:00 AM CDT. Meeting location: HQ building, 1100 N Mineral Springs Rd Porter, IN. Meet at the flagpole. 6. Initial pumping. Attachment 2 shows all listed sites pumped "upon award." Over what period does the Government expect that initial pumping to be completed? Answer: Within one month after receiving the BPA award. 7. For CLIN 0001, does one "EA" represent pumping of one individual septic or lift-station location, regardless of tank size, or may multiple scheduled locations be completed and billed as one service call? Answer: See question and answer #1. 8. The Scope of Work lists an estimated annual quantity of 20 routine pumpings, while Attachment 2 (Proposed Septic Pumping Schedule) appears to show 29 locations upon award and a materially higher total number of scheduled pumping events. Which quantity and schedule should offerors use as the basis for pricing and anticipated ordering? Answer: There are 25 tanks at 21 sites. Campground Douglas, Mather, and RV dump station are baffled and connected. So instead of two 2,000 gallon tanks, they are each one 4,000 gallon tank. The 20 Dorm septic tank has been bypassed; there is a lift station there that pumps directly to city sewer. 9. Please provide, if available, the estimated volumes for Mt. Baldy Secondary and Preschool (Wahl Farm), as well as estimated lift-station volumes referenced in Attachment 2 (Proposed Septic Pumping Schedule). Answer: Mt. Baldy Secondary estimate is 1,500 gallons. Preschool (Wahl Farm) estimate is 1,000 gallons. Typical lift station volume is 500-750 gallons. 10. For pipe-cleaning and heavy-cleaning CLINs, please clarify the expected scope and unit of measure, including whether pricing is per location or per service call and any anticipated line lengths or equipment requirements. Answer: Like septic pumping, pricing should be determined by a base (callout) rate plus length of pipe to be cleaned. Routine cleaning being material removable by standard hydraulic jetting, while heavy cleaning would require multiple passes, mechanical cutting/descaling, specialized tooling, or debris removal beyond normal jetting. 11. Is there an incumbent contractor and, if so, may the Government provide prior-year call/order quantities by service category? Answer: There is no incumbent contractor. In a typical year, the Government has scheduled roughly 20 routine, two urgent, and four emergency pumps. Submit all questions only via email to james_bissaillon@ios.doi.gov. Quotes are due by 12:00 PM CDT on September 17, 2026, unless changed by solicitation amendment. Remember to monitor the solicitation posting for any amendments posted until the solicitation closes. All amendments must be acknowledged by the due date and time for quotes.

description: AMENDMENT FIVE - SPECS ADDED (ATTACHMENT 11) and GOVT RESPONSE TO ADDITIONAL CONTRACTOR QUESTIONS (ATTACHMENT 12) AMENDMENT FOUR - UPDATE ATTACHMENT 1 - BID SCHEDULE AMENDMENT THREE - GOVT RESPONSE TO CONTRACTOR QUESTIONS, ADD CLAUSE, ADD SUBMITALS AMENDMENT TWO - EXTEND BID DATE TO 17 SEP 2026 AT 2:00 PM. SITE VISIT ATTENDEES SHEET ADDED TO ATTACHMENTS AMENDMENT ONE - update RFQ, adds 2 attachments, clarifies items SITE VISIT 9/1/2026 - SEE ATTACHMENTS FLETC is required to adhere to Executive Order 14111 and the Interagency Security Committee (ISC) requirements for the physical security of federal facilities, which mandate robust perimeter protection in accordance with established standards. The currently installed perimeter security fence is non-compliant with anti-climb, anti-scale, and anti-crash ratings, creating a significant security vulnerability for the campus and its occupants. To address this risk and ensure compliance with ISC guidelines, the FLETC Chief Security Office (CSO) proposes the upgrade and replacement of the existing fencing with an approved perimeter fence designed and constructed in accordance with ISC, DHS, and FLETC physical security requirements, and in accordance with ASTM F2656 M30/P1, which specifies the impact resistance required to mitigate vehicle-borne threats. Implementing a perimeter fence will provide continuous, passive protection, eliminate the operational vulnerabilities associated with active barriers, and align the facility with current federal security standards.

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is offering for sale six (6) Items totaling three hundred twelve (312) acres located within the boundaries of the Fort Drum Military Installation, Fort Drum, New York of which approximately the following volumes to be harvested: All Items are being sold per unit harvested timber will be sold by WEIGHT & any sawlogs paid on Fort Drum Sliding Scale ITEM #s (1, 4, & 5) - Harvest Operations & Tree Cutting Dates 15 October 2026 - 15 April 2027 (3) - Harvest Operations & Tree Cutting Dates 15 October 2026 to 28 February 2027 All processing of wood on the log landings, skid trails/log landing repair, and cleanup must be complete by 31 August 2027. Designated timber harvested for removal within the items SHALL be skid to the log landings up to 15 May 2027 as long as all designated trees are cut by the 15 April 2027 tree cutting end date and there is continued disturbance through until completion generally not exceeding 30 days. Tree cutting is allowed from 15 October 2026 - 15 April 2027. Skidding and processing will be allowed after 15 April as long as all designated trees are cut by the 15 April 2027 tree cutting end date. Trees to be harvested within the items are designated either for removal or retention. The boundaries of the harvest areas are designated with blue �Timber Harvest Boundary� flagging with the exception of when along tank trail roads where common boundary is shared. Skid trails will be designated with yellow flagging and routed to avoid and limit cutting of residual unmarked trees as such designated for retention. Log landing size and location will be designated by agreement between the Purchaser and the District Representative. Care will be taken to avoid and minimize any damage to trees that are less than six inches (6�) Diameter at Breast Height and desirable growing stock as well as all designated leave trees. All unusable timber fiber (i.e. tops and bark) shall be used to stabilize skid trails and when not needed for trails piled on the log landing in a single pile. There is NO chipping requirement for this harvest. Purchaser SHALL avoid off-limits cultural sites, which are identified in the filed with pink/black striped flagging. There is no known excessive military metal contamination, however encountering military metal embedded within trees is still possible. ITEM #s (2 & 6) - Harvest Operations & Tree Cutting Dates 15 October 2026 - 15 April 2027 & 15 October 2027 � 15 April 2028 All processing of wood on the log landings, skid trails/log landing repair, and cleanup must be complete by 31 August 2028. Designated timber harvested for removal within the items SHALL be skid to the log landings up to 15 May 2028 as long as all designated trees are cut by the 15 April 2028 tree cutting end date and there is continued disturbance through until completion generally not exceeding 30 days. Tree cutting is allowed from 15 October 2026 - 15 April 2027 & 15 October 2027 � 15 April 2028. Skidding and processing will be allowed after 15 April as long as all designated trees are cut by the 15 April 2028 tree cutting end date. Trees to be harvested within the items are designated either for removal or retention. The boundaries of the harvest areas are designated with blue �Timber Harvest Boundary� flagging with the exception of when along tank trail roads where common boundary is shared. Skid trails will be designated with yellow flagging and routed to avoid and limit cutting of residual unmarked trees as such designated for retention. Log landing size and location will be designated by agreement between the Purchaser and the District Representative. Care will be taken to avoid and minimize any damage to trees that are less than six inches (6�) Diameter at Breast Height and desirable growing stock as well as all designated leave trees. All unusable timber fiber (i.e. tops and bark) shall be used to stabilize skid trails and when not needed for trails piled on the log landing in a single pile. There is NO chipping requirement for this harvest. Purchaser SHALL avoid off-limits cultural sites, which are identified in the filed with pink/black striped flagging. title: DHS - FLETC - GLYNCO - FENCE UPGRADE
description: AMENDMENT SIX - SALLY PORT GATE CLARIFICATION (ATTACHMENT 13) AMENDMENT FIVE - SPECS ADDED (ATTACHMENT 11) and GOVT RESPONSE TO ADDITIONAL CONTRACTOR QUESTIONS (ATTACHMENT 12) AMENDMENT FOUR - UPDATE ATTACHMENT 1 - BID SCHEDULE AMENDMENT THREE - GOVT RESPONSE TO CONTRACTOR QUESTIONS, ADD CLAUSE, ADD SUBMITALS AMENDMENT TWO - EXTEND BID DATE TO 17 SEP 2026 AT 2:00 PM. SITE VISIT ATTENDEES SHEET ADDED TO ATTACHMENTS AMENDMENT ONE - update RFQ, adds 2 attachments, clarifies items SITE VISIT 9/1/2026 - SEE ATTACHMENTS FLETC is required to adhere to Executive Order 14111 and the Interagency Security Committee (ISC) requirements for the physical security of federal facilities, which mandate robust perimeter protection in accordance with established standards. The currently installed perimeter security fence is non-compliant with anti-climb, anti-scale, and anti-crash ratings, creating a significant security vulnerability for the campus and its occupants. To address this risk and ensure compliance with ISC guidelines, the FLETC Chief Security Office (CSO) proposes the upgrade and replacement of the existing fencing with an approved perimeter fence designed and constructed in accordance with ISC, DHS, and FLETC physical security requirements, and in accordance with ASTM F2656 M30/P1, which specifies the impact resistance required to mitigate vehicle-borne threats. Implementing a perimeter fence will provide continuous, passive protection, eliminate the operational vulnerabilities associated with active barriers, and align the facility with current federal security standards.

description: This is a NAVSUP WSS Philadelphia presolicitation notice for the repair of three (3) items for a five (5) year period estimated from 2027 through 2032 for the evaluation and repairs of various repair components of the Navy Weapon Systems in support of the F-18 aircraft. This is a combined Navy and FMS requirement. The items covered are: 1) NIIN 015830123 / Part Number 2028844-032, 2) NIIN 015830119 / Part Number 2030584-001, and 3) NIIN 016281388 / Part Number 2030584-002. The Government intends to solicit a Requirements Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) with DRS Training & Control Systems, LLC (12339). Even though these items are sole source to DRS Training & Control Systems, LLC, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. The subject items requires Government source approval prior to contract award. Only the source previously approved by the Government for repair of these items will be solicited. The time required for approval of a new source is normally such that an award cannot be delayed pending approval of a new source. If you are not an approved source you must submit, together with your proposal, the information detailed in the NAVSUP WSS Source Approval Information Brochure for Repair. This brochure identifies technical data required to be submitted based on your company�s experience in repair of the same or similar items. Additional information for submitting a Source Approval Request package can be obtained at: https://www.navsup.navy.mil/NAVSUP-Enterprise/NAVSUP-Weapon-Systems-Support/Business-Opps/ If your request for source approval is currently being evaluated at the NAVSUP WSS, submit a copy of the cover letter, which forwarded your request for source approval, with your offer. title: 9-Mile Pump Station
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District, in partnership with the Macomb County Public Works (MCPW), is seeking contractors for a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) construction contract for the 9-Mile Pump Station project located in St. Clair Shores, Macomb County, Michigan. The project entails constructing a new 9-Mile Pump Station to separate the 8-1/2 Mile Relief Drain from the 9-Mile Drain. Operating under an 880-day Period of Performance, this effort is designed to significantly reduce flood risks for southeast Michigan residents and better protect the water quality of Lake St. Clair.
